HUBSPOT COMPANY RECORD (Redwood Inference)

Account snapshot
- Regulated enterprise prospect (insurance / claims processing + customer service). Very security-led evaluation.
- Primary interest: Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated capacity if Private timeline slips. Hosted API considered only for non-sensitive workloads (public knowledge base).
- Buying committee includes CISO org + data governance + platform engineering.

Contacts (names redacted in CRM export)
- Director, AI Platform (technical champion) — wants consistent inference economics + region flexibility.
- VP, Infrastructure — pushing for VPC deployment and strict network controls.
- CISO / Vendor Risk — gating item; heavy emphasis on auditability + retention.

Use case / workload notes
- Phase 1: internal claims note summarization + call transcript summarization (chat-style generation). Input: 2–12k tokens typical, with spikes.
- Phase 2: adjuster assistant (RAG over policy + procedure docs) + embeddings for doc search.
- Latency targets (stated): “<2s to first token for interactive flows; p95 under ~8–10s for a 500–900 token answer.”
- Throughput: initial pilot ~50–150 concurrent sessions during peak; larger if rolled out to call center.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Their platform lead explicitly asked for something they can explain to procurement: “token cost is not enough — we need end-to-end latency/$ and what levers move it.”

Security / compliance requirements (from calls + emailed checklist)
- SSO/SAML: Required for console access; prefer Okta.
- Audit logging: Required (admin actions + access logs). Must be exportable to their SIEM (Splunk). They asked specifically about: API key creation/rotation, model version changes, routing policy changes, and user access events.
- Retention controls: Strong requirement. Want configurable retention for logs + the ability to set hard deletion windows. Stated target: 400+ days retention for some audit artifacts.
- Key management: KMS integration required (customer-managed keys for encryption at rest). Asked about envelope encryption and key rotation.
- Data residency: US-only processing for sensitive workloads. May add EU requirement for affiliate later; asked how we handle multi-region routing without violating residency.
- “No training on our data” clause required + confirmation in writing.
- Network: VPC deployment preferred; private connectivity options requested (PrivateLink/VPN). No inbound public endpoints for Private.
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 report requested; ISO 27001 certificate requested (or roadmap/timeline if not available).

Benchmark report tie-in (important)
- They are very interested in the public benchmark report for production economics but will not circulate it internally without the Security & Data Handling FAQ attached.
- Action item from last call: always send benchmark materials as a bundle:
  1) Benchmark report PDF/landing page link
  2) Security & Data Handling FAQ (Redwood-approved)
  3) Short note: what is measured, what is not, and explicit disclaimer that no customer data/logs are published.

Stage notes (Evaluation)
- They are past generic discovery; actively comparing deployment + security posture across vendors.
- They want to run a limited proof of concept inside a controlled environment (VPC), with their own prompts + redacted sample data.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-02-04: Inbound via website form after reading performance/latency content; requested “proof of economics” and security posture.
- 2025-02-06: Discovery call (30m) with Stephanie Nguyen + Markus Klein. Main takeaway: VPC/Private required for real workloads; hosted acceptable only for non-sensitive experiments.
- 2025-02-10: Sent initial follow-up with product overview + high-level architecture notes. They replied requesting audit logs + retention detail.
- 2025-02-13: Security intake started (their vendor risk form). Requested SOC 2, ISO27001, data handling statement, and audit log sample.
- 2025-02-18: Technical deep dive (45m) with Markus. Questions focused on: where logs live, what can be disabled, how routing is controlled, and how we guarantee region pinning.
- 2025-02-20: Champion asked for the benchmark report link + requested we include the security FAQ “so I don’t get blocked by GRC.”

Open questions from prospect
- Can we export audit logs to Splunk via webhook or periodic S3 export (or equivalent) in Private?
- Can they configure retention separately for request/response payloads vs metadata? (They prefer no payload logging by default.)
- Can they enforce model allowlists + block model changes without change control?
- How do we document that benchmarks do not use customer data and do not expose per-request traces?

Internal guidance / talk track
- Keep claims grounded: focus on methodology transparency and reproducibility. Do not claim universal superiority.
- Emphasize:
  - Private deployment + customer-controlled networking
  - Configurable logging/retention
  - Audit logs for administrative actions
  - Region pinning / residency controls
  - “No customer data in published benchmarks” + no raw per-request logs published

Next steps (owner)
- Stephanie to send: benchmark report + Security & Data Handling FAQ together (single email) + offer to walk through FAQ.
- Markus to schedule a 60-min security deep dive with their CISO team to cover audit logging, retention controls, KMS, and residency.
- If security team agrees on baseline controls, propose a 2-week POC plan (VPC) with success criteria: p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and operational logging requirements.

Notes / direct quotes
- CISO (paraphrased): “We can’t have black-box inference. We need audit trails, retention controls, and a clear statement about what data you store.”
- AI Platform Director: “Benchmarks are useful, but only if we can explain the methodology and the security posture in the same packet.”
